findings.issue: No test exercises tableWritesSettled (A-2, D-4, edge case 'Home while hand 10's write is still running'). Making it return Promise.resolve() or dropping it from App's Home effect would leave every test green.
findings.evidence: SPEC-02 polls storedSessions until handsPlayed is 10 before clicking Home (e2e/home-control.spec.ts:153), and SPEC-07 (1) polls until the start record exists before Back (e2e/history.spec.ts:76). So the read never races a pending write. Spec section 7 says the 0-hands case is covered by 'SPEC-07 (1) via Back', but the poll before Back stops that from happening. The spec's own SPEC items do ask for the wait, so this is a gap in coverage, not a SPEC violation.
findings.fix: Add one browser check that clicks Home or Back while a write is still pending. For example, use an init script that wraps IDBObjectStore.prototype.put/add on the 'sessions' store and delays the transaction (or holds the request until a flag is set). Click Home, assert data-paused stays 'loading' until the write is released, then assert the subtitle shows the new count. Or, in SPEC-07 (1), press Back right after Start game with the start put held back, and assert '0 hands'.

findings.issue: The history key comes from performance.timeOrigin. That holds in production but is why SPEC-07 (5) has to drop the paused clock that every other case uses.
findings.evidence: Production: the key from an earlier load can only match if a later load of the same tab has the same timeOrigin at the browser's precision and the same counter. Precision is about 100 us in Chromium and 1 ms in Safari and Firefox, and up to about 100 ms with Firefox resistFingerprinting. A reload that follows a Start game click can't start that soon after the load that pushed the entry. bfcache restores the same document, so the counter, tableKey ref and history.state still agree. Duplicate tab, session restore and tab discard all start a new load with a new timeOrigin. So the key is sound. Under Playwright's page.clock.install, timeOrigin is the same on every load, so keys collide. That is a harness artefact, and the builder's real-clock case (5) handles it correctly. Case (5) still discriminates: a counter-only key would make Back do nothing there and fail the test. Running Chromium and WebKit on the real clock does prove the cross-load behaviour.
findings.fix: Optional, and only with a spec note since D-2 fixes the key format: build the key from crypto.getRandomValues, as newSessionId already does, or from crypto.randomUUID. Then the key no longer depends on the clock and case (5) can run under the paused clock like the others. Otherwise leave it as is.

findings.issue: After Back on the Table then Forward (ignored, so Home sits on the stale T1 entry), the next Back on Home goes to the app's own entry in the same document and nothing visible happens. A second Back is needed to leave the app.
findings.evidence: Rule 3's sequence [app, T1*] on Home: popstate(null) runs while tableKey is null and is ignored. That matches the approved D-2 rule 'any other popstate is ignored', so it is spec-conformant.
findings.fix: None required. If wanted, call history.back() once more when a Table-entry popstate arrives while on Home, or mention the double Back in docs/ui/navigation.md.

summary: All 12 SPEC items are implemented as specified and every rubric line passes. There are no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. The header markup, the nextBotName cap, the no-write pause, the write chain and the D-2 history handling all match the spec, and the tests assert the specified values. On the disputed D-2 key: performance.timeOrigin plus the counter is sound in production (bfcache keeps the same document, and separate loads cannot share a timeOrigin at real precisions). The collision exists only under Playwright's fake clock. SPEC-07 (5) on the real clock still proves the cross-load behaviour and would fail with a counter-only key. One MINOR: no test exercises tableWritesSettled, so the A-2 race fix could be removed without any test failing.
